title: Pagetoid reticulosis and its differential diagnoses: a multicenter, retrospective, non-interventional study describing the histological and clinical criteria
summary:
Pagetoid reticulosis is a rare skin condition in which white blood cells (lymphocytes) proliferate within the skin. The diagnosis is based on the microscopic and clinical findings, i.e., the characteristics of the skin lesions. The course of the disease is benign; however, distinguishing it from potentially life-threatening neoplastic diseases can be difficult in some cases, particularly since the conditions cannot always be differentiated microscopically.

The aim of this study is to compile cases from multiple participating centers and describe new characteristics that should facilitate diagnosis in the future.

To this end, we will collect and describe tissue samples and clinical data from patients with pagetoid reticulosis and aggressive lymphomas to gain new insights into the disease course and define new criteria for diagnosing the condition.

interventions.name: This is a multicenter study. Diagnostic slides and formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue samples from representative lesions of patients with Paget-like reticulosis will be retrieved from the archives of the Department of Microscopic Dermatology at Charité or from the (dermato-)pathology archives

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    Adult patients for whom skin tissue samples are archived at the respective participating center.
-    Lymphoproliferative disease of the skin with histologically evident so-called “Pagetoid” epidermotropism, as is typical of Pagetoid reticulosis. In addition to Pagetoid reticulosis, the following entities in particular are considered and included: Mycosis fungoides, lymphomatoid papulosis type D, primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma, primary cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma, primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS 
-	The diagnosis must be confirmed by clinical-pathological correlation, and the course of the disease must be traceable for at least 6 months
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under the age of 18
